title: A binary search tree and its four traversals

blocks.text: In a **binary search tree** every node's left subtree holds smaller values and its right subtree larger ones. The page walks one tree in four orders: in-order (left, root, right) gives the values sorted, pre-order puts the root first, post-order puts it last, and **level order** goes breadth-first, one level at a time, with a queue.

items: `insert(value)` places a value; **a value already in the tree is ignored**; `null` is refused with `NullPointerException`.
`height()` is the number of edges on the longest root-to-leaf path: one node has height 0 and **an empty tree has height -1**.

cases.says: After inserting 5, 3, 7, 1, 4 the four traversals give the page's four lists, and the tree's height is 2.
Inserting a value the tree already holds changes nothing, so the in-order list has no repeats.
On a tree three levels deep, level order lists every node of a level before any node of the next level.
An empty tree gives four empty lists and a height of -1; a single node has height 0.

concepts: A tree's height counts edges on its longest root-to-leaf path, so one node has height 0 and an empty tree -1.
In a binary search tree in-order traversal gives sorted values, pre-order puts the root first, post-order last, and level order goes breadth-first with a queue.
